data.narrative:
Zanskar is a Series C climate and energy company founded by Carl Hoiland and Joel Edwards that has raised $180M to date. Valuation analysis draws from a comparable set of 9 private peers and 1 public company (LNZA) in the Climate & Energy sector. The three primary private comparables—KoBold Metals ($3.0B), Electric Hydrogen ($1.0B), and Amogy ($700M)—span a wide range reflective of high dispersion in this emerging sector.

Two triangulation methods are applicable. The Stage-Progression method applies a typical 1.7x step-up multiplier to the $180M total raised proxy, implying a valuation of $306M. The Peer-Median method identifies a $1.0B median valuation across the three same-stage, same-sector comparables, with observed peer valuations ranging from $700M to $3.0B. This wide range reflects meaningful heterogeneity in market assessment of climate-tech maturity and capital intensity.

Synthesis of both methods produces a triangulated range of $260M (low) to $1.1B (high), with a median of $653M. The Stage-Progression method anchors the lower bound, while Peer-Median—given the presence of higher-valued peers—anchors the upper bound. Key uncertainties include the appropriate discount or premium to peer medians based on Zanskar's specific technology, unit economics, and path to commercialization, alongside inherent volatility in private climate-tech valuations.
